newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks leap on HSBC strength, post record close.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks leap on HSBC strength, post record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks soared on Thursday to a record close on continued strength of HSBC Holdings, although profit-taking in the afternoon trimmed intra-day gains, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index finished up 260.27 points, or 1.69 percent, at 15,706.29 after hitting an all-time intra-day high of 15,783.27 in the morning session.
"The rally is principally fuelled by HSBC Holdings, and properties were steadier," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
HSBC surged HK$15.00 to close at all-time high of HK$279.
The stock was lifted by optimism on banks in London and hopes of solid interim earnings due on August 4, brokers said.
"People are buying (HSBC) ahead of its result announcement and nobody is willing to sell now," a local broker said.
The blue-chip index smashed its previous intra-day record of 15,635.52 set on July 16 within minutes after the opening and gained as much as 337 points before profit-taking set in.
"The Hang Seng Index has broken above its long-term uptrend channel. It can push up to 16,000 maybe over the next two weeks," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.

Brokers said the short term market trend would depended on liquidity. "We saw some Chinese money flowing into the market snapping up blue chips since the Hong Kong market is cheap when compared with the Chinese market," one broker said.
Property counters were steady to firmer after the market digested news that the government plans to increase land supply to calm spiraling housing prices.
Cheung Kong was unchanged at HK$75.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.25 to HK$89.75.
Shares of Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong, or H-shares, soared on hopes of corporate restructurings.
Investors bought H-shares on hopes that restructurings would be followed by asset injections, like red chips, Chia said.
The Hang Seng H-share index jumped 26.39 points, or 2.35 percent, to close at 1,151.67. Beiren surged HK$0.525 to HK$2.700 and Nanjing Panda rose HK$0.18 to HK$1.98.

Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI) rose HK$3.15 to HK$26.20 and China Resources added HK$0.80 to HK$36.30. CKI and China Resources were lifted by news they would be included in the blue-chip Hang Seng Index from August.
Overall market turnover was HK$22.83 billion compared to HK$21.71 billion on Wednesday.
